newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Quake jolts NZ's North Island, no damage.
newsitem.headline: Quake jolts NZ's North Island, no damage.

text.p: A strong earthquake jolted New Zealand's lower North Island early on Saturday, the second in three days, but there were no reports of serious damage.
The quake, centred close to one on Thursday night, began about 3.40 a.m. (1540 GMT Friday) with a sharp jolt followed by tremors lasting about 20 seconds.
The Institute of Geological and Nuclear Sciences said the quake measured 5.2 on the Richter scale, and was centred 30 km (19 miles) northwest of Wellington at a depth of 30 km.
It was felt most strongly in the Kapiti Coast, north of the capital, and Wanganui on the island's central western coast, but emergency services received no reports of serious damage.
Thursday's night's jolt was of a similar magnitude and position.
Institute seismologist Ken Gledhill said the quake was a normal occurrence for Wellington.
